name: Reda El Maazi
headline: AI for Solopreneurs | Partnered with Replit and Luma AI

sections.bio:
I help business owners use AI to remove boring tasks so they save time and focus on making more money.

I’ve worked with AI companies like Replit and Luma.

posts.text:
Just found out I ranked # 13 in Canada for creators talking about entrepreneurship on LinkedIn (Favikon Ranking). 🤩 

Honestly I did not see that coming.

I come from 10 years in tech recruiting and helping tech professionals land six figure jobs.

Now I work with small and medium businesses, same skills, same energy, just on the B2B side. And honestly I am having a blast.

The digging, the strategy, helping people figure out how to grow, I just love doing that stuff!

I am adding AI on top of it now and my goal is to help business owners use what they already have, move faster, and grow their business in a plug-and-play way.

If that sounds like something you are into, follow along. 

Thanks for being here!!🙏

I don't have a team. But I still know what my 6 closest competitors did overnight:

Yesterday, I showed how my AI agent scans my industry while I sleep. Last night, it tracked my competitors by name.

Same report. Same morning cappuccino. 

This time: 6 competitors watched every night.
Here's what it found:

- One is replacing 5 tools with a single AI tool.
- One built an AI helper that writes his LinkedIn posts.
- One has posted an AI demo every day for 479 days straight (!)

6 competitors (real ones). 

One AI agent. 

No hours spent digging through updates.

What should I have it watch next?

You have no idea what happened in your industry last night.
But that's about to change.

Here's what changed in my industry:

- AI workflow costs dropped 60%
- People don't want training anymore. They want it done for them.
- The word "agency" is dying. Everyone is moving to "partner" or "consultant."

Track this, and you're already two steps ahead.

I know because my AI agent checks every night while I sleep. 

It watches what competitors post, what they charge, and how they talk about their work.

Before, I did this by hand. 

Hours of scrolling, spreadsheets, guessing. 
Now it's one report, over cappuccino.

What would you want waiting on your desk every morning?

Yesterday, I joined the MP for Hochelaga and Parliamentary Secretary for Small Business for a 1-year citizenship anniversary event in Montreal.
Merci beaucoup Marie-Gabrielle Menard!

It made me look back at how this all started:

When I arrived in Canada in 2014, I had no network, no plan, and absolutely no one to call.

Today, my days are spent on the ground with Canadian business owners from Montreal to Vancouver.

We sit down, look at their businesses, and solve the operational challenges holding them back.

It is a deeply human job.

To everyone who opened a door, made an introduction, or simply believed this was possible, thank you.

I am incredibly grateful to be here and to have the opportunity to give back to the business community every day.

Spent last night at an EY event in Montreal with MAX - Muslims Achieving Excellence Network

One thing stood out:

Big companies have the resources, the brand, the relationships, and access to incredible talent.

Every move goes through stakeholders, forecasts, approval chains, and risk management.

Solopreneurs don't have those advantages. 
But you have something else: speed!

You can test an idea on Monday, get feedback on Tuesday, and change direction by Wednesday.

Most experiments and projects won't work. But a few will.

That speed compounds over time. 

When the market moves this fast, shipping fast is the biggest advantage.
